solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Composer's part upset matchless fellow

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach is the composer; the 's links him to the next piece

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: Someone trying to play a composer's piece makes a hash of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matchless' reads as 'unrivalled' but means without a wife; 'upset' turns the part around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A man without a match, i.e. without a wife, is an unmarried man.

clue.text: Card game in which universal inclination for fraud

indicators.note: the following letter is placed inside the card game's name

parts.note: monte is a gambling card game, as in three-card monte
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
a bank is a slope or incline

explanation.surface: A card game where a general tendency towards cheating is built in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank is a charlatan, a swindling quack or trickster.

clue.text: Where one is misused in general

indicators.note: words that are misused are put to the wrong use, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar point: where a word gets wrongly used in general speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' reads as 'generally' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the US Army general who led the Allied forces in Europe in WWII.

clue.text: Pulse started with heart bypass

indicators.note: a bypass skips the heart, so the central letter of the word is left out

parts.note: started means began

explanation.surface: Someone's pulse started up again after heart bypass surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and a bean is one such seed.

clue.text: Value in warmth and love in republic

parts.note: a tog is the unit for the warmth value of a duvet or garment
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A nation that prizes warmth and love.
explanation.walkthrough: TOG is a British unit rating how warm a duvet is.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African country with a republican government.

clue.text: Landowner wasting day in retreat

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the letter for day is dropped

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A landowner squandering a day withdrawing from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is a Scottish estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is its hideaway, a place to withdraw to.

clue.text: Info gathered in order to make engine part

indicators.note: the info word is collected inside the word for order

parts.note: a bid is an order or command, as in 'do my bid'
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A mechanic gathers information to build a part of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of a connecting rod, joined to the crankshaft in a piston engine.

clue.text: Awakening back when given to religious instruction

indicators.note: back means the letters for when are read in reverse

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A spiritual awakening that came back when someone took up religious study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AS into SA; 'given' only links it to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden enlightenment.

clue.text: In time soon over obsessive self-love

indicators.note: over means the whole assembly is turned around and read backwards
in places the word for soon inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
in a mo is British slang for soon, short for in a moment

explanation.surface: Someone will soon be over an obsession with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts INAMO into AGE to make AINAMOGE; 'over' turns that back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an excessive, obsessive preoccupation with oneself.

clue.text: Endless crack in part of mug

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a chink is a narrow crack or gap

explanation.surface: A crack running round part of a coffee mug.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug is slang for face, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for the face, and the jaw's lower point is a feature of it.

clue.text: Dane rambling on about cheese writer

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so these letters are rearranged
about means the word on goes round the cheese

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A Dane goes on and on about cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' signals the anagram of the Dane; 'about' puts the word on around the cheese. The writer's surname carries an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna O'Brien was an Irish novelist, author of The Country Girls.

clue.text: Down and dirty

definitions.meaning: down here means sad or depressed
dirty in the sense of smutty or risqué, as in a racy joke

explanation.surface: Feeling low and grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word serves both as feeling sad and as smutty or indecent.

clue.text: He pens new book to contribute on gold mineral

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the other pieces are held between the letters of He

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters H and E

indicators.note: on means the following pieces come after the gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
to lend is to contribute or give

explanation.surface: A man writes a new book to add to the literature on gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means encloses; OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornblende is a dark rock-forming silicate mineral of the amphibole group.

clue.text: Official tempted woman after scripture class

indicators.note: after means the woman comes behind the class

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
Eve was tempted by the serpent in Genesis

explanation.surface: An official tempted a woman after a Bible lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or administrative officer in medieval England.

clue.text: Struggled again losing thousand in racket

parts.note: struggled means battled

indicators.note: losing means the letter for thousand is dropped

parts.note: more means again, as in 'once more'
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone struggled once more after losing a thousand on a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a scam but is the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the small bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock.

clue.text: English setter, say, barking in comfortable situation

indicators.note: barking means mad in British slang, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An English setter dog barking while lounging in comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKING is British slang for crazy, hence the anagram; the setter is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort and affluence.

clue.text: Song Frau von Trapp won't start

indicators.note: won't start means the first letter of her name is omitted

parts.note: Maria von Trapp is the heroine of The Sound of Music

explanation.surface: Maria from The Sound of Music refuses to begin singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in opera.

clue.text: Grain's item removed from chicken or veal?

indicators.note: removed from means the word item is taken out of the meat

parts.note: chicken and veal are examples of white meat, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A grain is taken out of a dish of chicken or veal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal crop, harvested for its seed.

clue.text: Second rescue boat finds island

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A second lifeboat reaches an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: Grass full of hypocrisy renounced former practice

indicators.note: full of means the hypocrisy word sits inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: An informer full of hypocrisy turned away from old habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for an informer, but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a belief or opinion formerly held.

clue.text: Pan's character's gypsy taking call

indicators.note: taking means the call follows on, joined to the gypsy

parts.note: tinker was an old term for an itinerant gypsy or traveller
a bell is a ring, a call on the phone

explanation.surface: A character in a Pan story is a traveller answering a call.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan is named Tinker Bell.

clue.text: Sun exposed this high-flier's mistake

parts.note: in Greek myth a boy flew too near the sun on wings of wax, which melted, so the sun showed up his folly

explanation.surface: A tabloid like The Sun exposing a high-flying executive's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which makes the clue read as a scandal story.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Daedalus flew too close to the sun, his wax wings melted and he fell.

clue.text: Push wine level

definitions.meaning: to give someone the push is to dismiss them
an old name for dry white fortified wine like sherry
to raze or plunder a town

explanation.surface: Pressing down on the wine lever.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as dismissal, as an old fortified Spanish wine, and as plundering a town.

clue.text: Shark attack experienced involving sweetheart

parts.note: to hammer is to attack fiercely

indicators.note: involving means the experienced word includes the heart letter

parts.note: had means experienced, as in 'had a fright'
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A shark attack experienced by someone's loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammerhead is a shark with a flattened, mallet-shaped head.

clue.text: Beer leads to melee in local diner

indicators.note: leads are the front letters, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Beer leads to a brawl in a pub restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Local is British for the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild is a dark, lightly hopped British ale.

clue.text: Tease European showing violent emotion

parts.note: to rag is to tease

explanation.surface: Teasing a European provokes an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is intense, violent anger.

clue.text: Constant smoker worried about inhaling gas

indicators.note: inhaling means taking the gas letter in
about means the worried word is turned round

parts.note: ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you'
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: A chain smoker, anxious about breathing in fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ATE into ETA, which takes in N. 'Smoker' is a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna, the Sicilian volcano, is almost always emitting smoke and ash.

clue.text: Control temperature for weakling

parts.note: to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: Regulating the heat for someone feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt of a litter is its smallest, weakest animal.

clue.text: Stew from two islands gran's right to decline

parts.note: Mull is a Scottish island and I abbreviates island

indicators.note: to decline means to refuse, so the right letter is dropped

parts.note: gran is grandmother; the 's links it

explanation.surface: Gran's island stew, which she won't let the family turn down.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL is an island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligan is an American stew made from whatever odds and ends are available.

clue.text: Smoking habit?

parts.note: a habit is a garment, and this jacket name is also slang for a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: A question about someone's addiction to cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is both a cannabis cigarette and a short double-breasted jacket worn by sailors.
